Q: Spring Boot: Field required a bean of type that could not be found A:

Reason : Spring JPA is unable to find bean/instance of CustomerRepository while compiling and starting the application.

use @Repository annotation, that will creating a bean of CustomerRepository during initialization. This annotation tells Spring to creating a bean during startup. Codewise, there will not be any syntax error, but Spring will not provide bean until it sees this annotation for e.g.

@Repository
public interface CustomerRepository extends CrudRepository<Customer, Long>

Further ensure to annotate @Entity @Table (class level) and @Id and @Column (field level) to you Customer class, otherwise it will further throw type error.

Q: docker compose build fails: 'unable to prepare context: unable to evaluate symlinks in context path: The system cannot find the path specified.' A:

It turns out moving the files to a dev drive and accessing it through a mounted volume would cause issues.

Prior to moving all my code, everything was under the $HOME/source/repos/... path. Unfortunately, a lot of my projects hardcode paths and must live here. Dev drives offer an option to access the drive through user defined paths and wanted to access through this path.


added my path here

Now I can access my projects through $HOME/source/repos/... or /d/repos/.... If I were to try to run docker compose commands through my home path, I would get the error.

To fix it, I MUST work with this project on the dev drive directly /d/repos/....

I think the volume mount isn't understood by docker and fails to see anything inside it. Fortunately for me, the projects that have the hardcoded paths are visual studio solutions and I'd expect that to work here (so far, no issues).

Q: How to COUNT() the related records in a JOINed table per parent table row using a MySQL query A:

Since you mention that you're unfamiliar with SQL joins, perhaps you'd find the Wikipedia article or the W3Schools lesson on the subject informative (these were the top 2 results when I searched Google for "SQL join").

Failing that, following the link about SUM() in the MySQL function reference takes one to a page on GROUP BY (Aggregate) functions, which is rather a strong hint towards the answer. 

SELECT channels.*, SUM(ip) AS visits
FROM
  channels JOIN log ON (
    log.module = 'channels' AND
    log.mid = channels.id -- or whatever is the appropriate column in `channels`
  )
GROUP BY log.mid;

Q: xlPasteValues and xlPasteFormats at the same time A:

Here the problem of efficiency, is that the worksheet must be searched twice for its' maximum range. This is the reason for, you want to use just one expression, but With can use the same range object. And Offset can use a built-in function, that is volatile, and it could slow down the working speed.

I also experienced such kind of lack of speed, when creating a new worksheet, either by copying the entire worksheet, or by creating an empty new one, and copy-pasting the content of an Excel range. And this is not just a problem of a VBA macro, I also tried to create manually the worksheet, and also took at least 42-43 seconds. Just setting the range, this is much faster afterwards.

One possible fix, can be finding a Paste option, that both copies cells formats and values as well. This could be the option xlPasteAllUsingSourceTheme, but the column widths would not be preserved. Instead, this may copy also formulas, and it should be combined with xlPasteColumnWidths option, whenever you want to keep exactly the formatting of the source worksheet.

ws16.Cells(Rows.Count, "B").End(xlUp).Offset(4, 0).PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteAllUsingSourceTheme

Or you can use With as follows, which is more efficient, than calling PasteSpecial in two lines, for a range, that would be obtained two times, in two separate calls.

With ws16.Cells(Rows.Count, "B").End(xlUp).Offset(4, 0)
.PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteFormats
.PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteValues
End With

Q: Spatially visualising single gene expression in a selected cell type using Seurat A:

I am not super experienced with Seurat's spatial functions, I usually use semla. For that package, the code could be:

# load package
library(semla)

# convert seurat object to a semla object, important for the tissue image
sem_obj <- UpdateSeuratForSemla(nano.obj_all)

# your subset, for the annotation labels you want to plot. 
sem_obj <- SubsetSTData(sem_object, expression = plot_group %in% c("epi", "stroma", "myeloids", "tcells", "plasmas"))

# assuming you want to plot something like nFeatures, or any other numeric value of the metadata. If you want to plot categorical feature, use MapLabels()
p <- MapFeatures(sem_obj, features = "nFeature_Spatial", image_use = "raw", pt_size = 0.6)

# save the plot
ggsave(p,...)

Q: How to develop software that contains more than 20,000 lines of code? A:

Usually, 20,000 LOC is achieved by a team of coders on big projects.

I'm working on code for a medical device and it has over 20,000 LOC. The language section for the display contains a lot of code, mostly tables.

We don't concern ourselves with LOC, except the per-file limit; we try to keep files lower than 1000 LOC. Our primary concern is safety and implementing the requirements, regardless of the LOC required.
